system.name: DeFT
system.one_liner: A hardware-efficient attention algorithm (Decoding with Flash Tree-attention) for tree-structured LLM inference, with prefix-aware, load-balanced KV cache partitions.

content.variant_note: four numbered mini decoding trees in one cream box, set under an unconnected sequence-based baseline and a colour key, all in one tall single column
content.argues: Many LLM workloads decode as trees whose shared prefixes (blue) could share one KV cache, unlike sequence-based decoding where every pair stands alone.
content.subject: Prompt and generation nodes of sequence-based decoding and of four tree-structured workloads, coloured by whether their KV cache is shareable.

lessons.what_to_learn: Define the node colours once in a Notations box (shareable versus non-shareable), then redraw the same node grammar for each application so the shared blue parts stand out across different tree shapes; put the sequential baseline above as unconnected pairs.
lessons.suits: systems or inference papers whose point is a structural property, such as shared prefixes or reuse, common to several workloads.

evidence: many applications are now designed to process sequences with an internal tree structure
We need a more efficient decoding algorithm in response to this interaction paradigm change from sequence-based decoding to tree-based decoding.
An illustration of Sequence-based decoding and Tree-based decoding.

summary: DeFT is a hardware-efficient attention algorithm for tree-structured LLM inference, where many generation calls share prefixes whose KV cache can be reused. Figure 1 sets sequence-based decoding, two unconnected prompt-generation pairs, above tree-based decoding. A Notations box defines blue as shareable KV cache, green as non-shareable prompt and yellow as non-shareable generation. A cream box then redraws these colours as four numbered mini trees: self-consistency, few-shot prompting, multi-step reasoning such as Tree-of-thoughts with search-history nodes, and speculative decoding, where pink block arrows show draft token-tree generation, verification and keeping the KV cache. Flat draw.io-style boxes and thin arrows in one tall single column carry the idea.
summary_zh: DeFT 面向树状 LLM 推理，核心是复用共享前缀的 KV 缓存。图1上方用两对互不相连的提示与生成表示序列式解码，下方在米色框中画出四种树状负载（自洽、少样本、多步推理、推测解码），蓝色节点表示可共享的 KV 缓存。
notes: Prior kinds scope-overview and side-by-side-contrast kept; variant changed from taxonomy-map to example-gallery because the four workloads are mini decoding trees, not a category tree; concept-schematic added for the structural idea. Panels: the four numbered workloads and the sequence-based box are counted; the Tree-based decoding box is their container and the Notations box is treated as a legend. The pink draft-token colour is not in the key. The idioms decoding-tree and shared-prefix-colouring are coined.
